newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo Bourse jumpS with Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Oslo Bourse jumpS with Wall Street.

text.p: Norwegian shares firmed on Friday after overnight gains on Wall Street as the Oslo Bourse continued to shadow U.S. stocks.
The Oslo Total index closed 1.22 percent higher at 941.39 points in heavy trade worth 1.3 billion crowns.

A dealer pointed out that the volume was inflated by several share options declared and a sell-off of by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and its parent, Deutsche Bank AG, of their 47.4 percent holdings in software company Sysdeco.
Sysdeco closed 1.76 percent higher at 17.30 crowns on the Oslo Bourse with 125 million crowns worth of shares changing hands. It was the second most traded share of the day.
Norwegian investor Christen Sveaas bought some of the shares in Sysdeco.
Industrial conglomerate Norsk Hydro spearheaded the upturn on the bourse, rising 1.54 percent to 330 crowns. At 168 million crowns, it was the most traded share of the day.
